title: Set the Stage
body: Change one cue that teaches people how to use a shared space.
notes: Draw on the published idea of culture surviving without a poster.
aria: Set the Stage. Change one cue that teaches people how to use a shared space.

title: Environment
body: Part III uses Chapters 14 and 16.
notes: Define the language and stage themes.
aria: Environment. Part III uses Chapters 14 and 16.

title: What the room teaches
body: Look at language, pace, stress and physical setup.
notes: Include a group chat as a shared space.
aria: What the room teaches. Look at language, pace, stress and physical setup.

title: Activity: choose an environment
body: Pick a meeting, team table or first-job station to audit.
notes: A fictional setting works.
aria: Activity: choose an environment. Pick a meeting, team table or first-job station to audit.

title: What you tolerate
body: Chapter 16 connects the environment with behavior people repeatedly allow.
notes: Use a repeated joke or missing tool. [BRENEN EXCERPT: 2–4 sentences from the mapped chapter, approved by Brenen]
aria: What you tolerate. Chapter 16 connects the environment with behavior people repeatedly allow.

title: The Stage
body: Compare a restaurant pickup station and a club sign-in table.
notes: Use a clearly labeled hypothetical restaurant example.
aria: The Stage. Compare a restaurant pickup station and a club sign-in table.

title: Activity: a newcomer's first ten minutes
body: List five observable features without taking pictures.
notes: Record what someone sees, hears or has to ask.
aria: Activity: a newcomer's first ten minutes. List five observable features without taking pictures.

title: What has been sliding?
body: Describe one tolerated behavior without assigning motives.
notes: Ask who has standing to change it.
aria: What has been sliding?. Describe one tolerated behavior without assigning motives.

title: Language sets the culture
body: Chapter 14 makes repeated language part of leadership practice.
notes: Compare a clear request with a cutting remark. [BRENEN EXCERPT: 2–4 sentences from the mapped chapter, approved by Brenen]
aria: Language sets the culture. Chapter 14 makes repeated language part of leadership practice.

title: A controlled response
body: Use a calm factual instruction during a rush.
notes: Distinguish composure from pretending everything is fine.
aria: A controlled response. Use a calm factual instruction during a rush.

title: The words that travel
body: Sarcasm about absent teammates and panic in a chat affect newcomers.
notes: Choose one phrase worth changing.
aria: The words that travel. Sarcasm about absent teammates and panic in a chat affect newcomers.

title: Activity: rewrite two lines
body: Replace two put-downs with specific requests.
notes: Keep the same operational problem.
aria: Activity: rewrite two lines. Replace two put-downs with specific requests.

title: Read rising stress
body: Stress can point to missing tools, unclear roles or a bottleneck.
notes: Avoid diagnosing a person. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: Read rising stress. Stress can point to missing tools, unclear roles or a bottleneck.

title: What to check first
body: A line at the supply table may reflect one shared pair of scissors.
notes: Look for a change that tests the explanation.
aria: What to check first. A line at the supply table may reflect one shared pair of scissors.

title: Mid-quiz: three decisions
body: Check tolerated behavior, language and a diagnostic response to stress.
notes: Explain answers with observable facts.
aria: Mid-quiz: three decisions. Check tolerated behavior, language and a diagnostic response to stress.

title: Pace, music and energy
body: Examine what helps people hear instructions and stay on task.
notes: Use a car wash, group chat or club meeting. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: Pace, music and energy. Examine what helps people hear instructions and stay on task.

title: A lever you control
body: Change one part of the environment you can influence.
notes: Ask permission before moving shared equipment. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.

title: Four review questions
body: Check tone, setup, energy and your own composure.
notes: Adapt the official after-action template. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: Four review questions. Check tone, setup, energy and your own composure.

title: Activity: score four checks
body: Give each check a rating from one to five and one observation.
notes: A number without an example is hard to interpret.
aria: Activity: score four checks. Give each check a rating from one to five and one observation.

title: Screen recording: a ten-minute reset
body: Plan a 6–10 minute walk of a table or station.
notes: Use annotated images of objects with no student faces until recorded.
aria: Screen recording: a ten-minute reset. Plan a 6–10 minute walk of a table or station.

title: A one-week experiment
body: Choose a tolerated behavior and a language habit to change.
notes: Specify when and how to observe both.
aria: A one-week experiment. Choose a tolerated behavior and a language habit to change.

title: Raise a standard privately
body: Correct a person's behavior away from the group under Chapter 18.
notes: Preview L4 without asking a peer to discipline others.
aria: Raise a standard privately. Correct a person's behavior away from the group under Chapter 18.

title: The group chat is a room
body: A pinned current link and a clear request can reduce repeated questions.
notes: Compare with a stream of sarcastic replies.
aria: The group chat is a room. A pinned current link and a clear request can reduce repeated questions.

title: A truthful process bullet
body: Describe the space you changed and the difference you observed.
notes: Use an actual prep station or club example only if true.
aria: A truthful process bullet. Describe the space you changed and the difference you observed.

title: Worksheet: Environment Audit and One-Week Change
body: Combine a newcomer list, four scores and two changes.
notes: Reserve space for the follow-up date.
aria: Worksheet: Environment Audit and One-Week Change. Combine a newcomer list, four scores and two changes.

title: Common traps
body: Decorating the room may leave an unclear handoff untouched.
notes: Separate a preference from a standard.
aria: Common traps. Decorating the room may leave an unclear handoff untouched.

title: What changed in the room?
body: Summarize the tolerated behavior, the language and the next check.
notes: Return to Chapters 14 and 16.
aria: What changed in the room?. Summarize the tolerated behavior, the language and the next check.

title: Next: everyday techniques
body: Introduce the huddle and private one-on-one.
notes: They are practiced in L4.
aria: Next: everyday techniques. Introduce the huddle and private one-on-one.

title: Optional completion record
body: Choose whether to transfer a true skill or completion line.
notes: Preview all text first.
aria: Optional completion record. Choose whether to transfer a true skill or completion line.

title: End question: the actual standard
body: Identify which behavior people tolerate in the scene.
notes: Explain how a newcomer would infer it.
aria: End question: the actual standard. Identify which behavior people tolerate in the scene.

title: End question: language under pressure
body: Choose a request that names the next useful action.
notes: Tie it to Chapter 14.
aria: End question: language under pressure. Choose a request that names the next useful action.

title: End question: stress as information
body: Look for a process that can be checked before blaming a peer.
notes: Use a sign-in queue.
aria: End question: stress as information. Look for a process that can be checked before blaming a peer.

title: End question: ten minutes to reset
body: Choose one fix within the student's role and time.
notes: Explain why reorganizing everything would obscure the test.
aria: End question: ten minutes to reset. Choose one fix within the student's role and time.

title: End question: a defensible resume claim
body: Compare a true station change with an inflated culture claim.
notes: Ask what evidence supports the result.

title: Answer review
body: Show why each choice fits the facts.
notes: Allow unlimited retries.

title: Try one change this week
body: Choose when to return and observe the difference.
notes: Bring the worksheet.
